sources_read: .qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r1/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx :: Quality Checks row 43 (#42 reward_ranking_is_monotone) and Internal Quality Checks row 43 incl. E43 annotation 'Mukesh - we need to monitor this one.'
evidence: Structural layer is monotone: scoring.toml (gates render/constraints = 0.0, weights functional 0.6/polish 0.2/visual 0.2, floor functional 0.05) and tools/score.py are byte-identical to the frozen template; reward = weighted mean only when every gate > 0 and functional > 0.05, all non-decreasing in every dimension score, so a dominating app can never score lower via weights/gates. Functional carries more mass than craft (0.6 vs 0.4). Functional criterion weights sum to 34.0 (1.5..3.0 each); gates are basic reachability/sign-in/reload checks a stronger app should not fail. However, a criterion inverts the ranking through shared state. tests/scored/functional/judge.toml criterion unread_and_new_messages_line (weight 2.0) says: 'Sign in as dev@kittle.test in two tabs ... Note M-13's unread count ... then as harriet post ... JUDGE-U1 and JUDGE-U2 ... In one tab Dev opens M-13: a "new messages" line sits just above JUDGE-U1'. The brief (environment/instructions/conversations.md 'Unread messages') says the line appears 'where I stopped reading', and the seed (environment/assets/kittle.json read_up_to) puts Dev's M-13 position at K-8. Seeded K-9 'Received, reading it tonight.' (Gwen, 2026-05-12T09:30, survives all timer changes) is after K-8, and earlier criteria in the listed order (nested_replies JUDGE-R0..R3/RX/R1B, edits_and_stale_edit JUDGE-E1) add more M-13 messages; no earlier criterion has Dev open M-13 (wall_every_route only reads Dev's list; wall_mentions_and_links uses M-11). So a correct app places the line above K-9, not above JUDGE-U1. The golden does exactly that: solution/app/public/app.js:185-187 sets newLineSeq to the first message with seq > last_read, and server.js:239-241 last_read comes from the seeded reads table. The scripted golden harness only passes because it adds an unstated pre-step: qc/repairs/kittle-2026-10-08/tests/functional.cjs:337 'await openMatter(dev, 'M-13'); await openMatter(dev, 'M-11');' before noting the count; the criterion text has no such step, so golden-run.log:16 'unread_and_new_messages_line PASS' does not exercise the criterion as written. Other observations (not inversions): cross-criterion dependencies (persistence on R0-R3/E1/H1; search_and_transcript on JUDGE-E1; deleted_message_takes_its_versions on timer_changes) compound penalties in the same direction only. Floor cliff: one 1.5-weight criterion alone = 1.5/34 = 0.044 < 0.05 floor -> reward 0 even with perfect craft, while one 2.0 criterion = 0.059 passes; this is monotone under dominance and template policy. Latent: wall_mentions_and_links requires posting '@Dev please review JUDGE-M1' in M-12; an app that refuses that post (a conforming reading of 'Nobody can be mentioned in a matter they can't see') could be failed as an unperformable step while a laxer app passes (P3, not adjudicated here). Runtime: raw-evidence-index.json states 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent'; no measured reward-ordering evidence exists, so risk stays true independent of the defect.
counterexample: Golden (correct) app: as written, the judge signs Dev in, notes M-13 count (>= 8: K-9 plus JUDGE-R0,R1,R2,R3,RX,R1B,E1), Harriet posts U1/U2, Dev opens M-13 and the golden renders 'New messages' above K-9 'Received, reading it tonight.' -> criterion fails (-2.0/34 functional, about -0.035 reward). Broken app B that ignores the seeded/persisted read positions and treats everything as read at Dev's sign-in (tracking only messages that arrived since) shows count 0 -> 2, line above JUDGE-U1, count 0 after opening, mark-unread works -> criterion passes. B is worse on the brief ('where I stopped reading', seeded read_up_to) yet outscores the golden on this 2.0-weight criterion.
suggested_fix: In unread_and_new_messages_line, add an explicit first step 'As dev@kittle.test open M-13 so it is read up to date, then open M-11' before noting the count (matching functional.cjs:337), or alternatively state the expected line as 'above the first message Dev had not read'; then rerun the scripted golden against the exact criterion text and record a reward-ordering measurement.
